data.title: CICT completes Asia Square Tower 2 sale, nets $12.4m fee
data.description:
It represented 0.5% of the Agreed Property Value.

CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust (CICT) has completed the sale of its 100% interest in Asia Square Tower 2, the trust's manager announced.

The completion follows CICT's divestment announcement dated 20 April and a subsequent announcement on 2 September relating to the exercise of the Call Option.

CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust Management Limited, as manager of CICT, elected to receive the divestment fee of approximately $12.4m, representing 0.5% of the Agreed Property Value, in cash.

The announcement was made by order of the board, signed by Company Secretaries Hon Wei Seng and Lee Wei Hsiung.

data.title: Retail investors net buy $888m in SG stocks through 16 September
data.description:
Net inflows rise to $4.02b, with DBS, OCBC, and SGX leading demand.

Retail investors net bought $888m worth of Singapore stocks over eight trading sessions through 16 September, following a new record high for the Straits Times Index, the SGX group said.

The STI reached 5,828.5 on 4 September, whilst the subsequent buying lifted cumulative retail net inflows for 2026 to $4.02b from $3.13b.

DBS Group Holdings, Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation, and Singapore Exchange accounted for around two-thirds of total retail net buying during the period.

SGX said the flows followed a first-half reporting season in which all three companies reported double-digit returns on equity.

Institutional investors moved in the opposite direction, with net selling widening by $163m over the eight sessions, it added.

Institutional buying strengthened in selected stocks including AEM Holdings, Yangzijiang Shipbuilding, Frencken Group, and Keppel.

Amongst small- and mid-cap stocks, ISDN recorded the highest retail net inflow relative to market capitalisation since 4 September.

The company had reported record first-half revenue and a 707% surge in profit attributable to shareholders.

Retail buying across the broader small- and mid-cap segment was concentrated in REITs and selected industrial stocks. 

SGX said REITs accounted for seven of the top 20 stocks by retail net inflow relative to market capitalisation, whilst SingPost, ComfortDelGro, and SATS were amongst the leading industrial names.

data.title: JTC, Kajima pilot autonomous heavy machinery in Jurong
data.description:
Excavator and compactor trials target 50% fewer skilled operators. 

JTC Corporation and Kajima Corporation have launched a pilot project to test autonomous heavy construction equipment at the Jurong Innovation District.

The trial will begin with excavators and compactors at the Bulim Autonomous Yard, JTC’s testing site for autonomous construction machinery.

An operator will assign tasks and set virtual geographic boundaries for each machine, which will then use sensors and artificial intelligence to carry out the work. 

The project targets a 50% reduction in the number of skilled operators required, keeping workers away from hazardous operating zones.

The autonomous excavator will use a retrofit system developed by Zurich-based Gravis Robotic.

Meanwhile, the compactor will run on Kajima’s A4CSEL autonomous construction system, its first deployment outside Japan.

JTC and Kajima also plan to explore adding autonomous bulldozers and dump trucks to the trial in 2027.

The pilot is being conducted with the Public Sector Science & Technology Policy & Plans Office and the Housing & Development Board.

data.title: HDB rents rise 1.6% YoY in August as monthly volumes slip
data.description:
Compared to July, HDB rental prices and volumes were lower.

HDB rental prices rose by 1.6% year-on-year (YoY) in August, with rents for both mature and non-mature estates being higher than a year ago, according to data from SRX and 99.co.

Rental prices for mature estates rose by 1.9% YoY, whilst non-mature estates’ rental prices climbed by 1.3% YoY.

Compared to July, HDB rental prices were slightly lower by 0.7%. Rental prices in mature and non-mature estates decreased by 0.5% and 0.1%, respectively.

An estimated 2,805 HDB flats were rented in August, higher by 1.3% year-on-year (YoY), but lower by 9.5% compared to the 3,099 HDB flats rented in July 2026.

4-room flats made up the largest share of rental volumes at 38.8%, followed by 3-room flags at 32.7%, 5-room flats at 23.5%, and executive flats at 5%.

data.title: Waymo joins ComfortDelGro, Grab as new local AV operator
data.description:
Initial manual driving is set to begin in 2027 ahead of commercial launch. 

Waymo will be Singapore’s newest autonomous vehicle operator, joining ComfortDelGro and Grab, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) announced.

Its autonomous vehicles are expected to arrive in the next few months, with initial manual driving to begin in 2027.

Waymo plans to launch commercial ride-hailing services in 2028.

LTA said it will work with the operator to ensure its deployments meet local safety and regulatory requirements.

It reiterated that autonomous vehicle deployment would not move ahead of its ability to retrain and support affected drivers.

“Building on the manpower transition package announced in July 2026, the government will continue to work closely with tripartite partners and operators to provide more support for drivers,” the LTA added.

data.title: Condo rents up 2.5% in August despite Ghost Month volume pullback
data.description:
Overall prices in all regions rose compared to the same month in 2025.

Condo rental prices rose 2.5% in August compared to a year earlier, whilst rental volumes expanded by 4.5%, according to data from SRX and 99.co.

Overall rental prices in the Core Central Region (CCR), Rest of Central Region (RCR), and Outside Central Region (OCR) rose by 3%, 2.2%, and 2% year-on-year, respectively.

Compared to July, overall condo rental prices were stable, said SRX and 99.co, with CCR and RCR prices inching up 0.7% and 0.6%, respectively, whilst OCR declined by 0.4%.

An estimated 8,318 units were rented in August, lower by 13.6% compared to the 9,627 condos rented in July.

Rental volumes were higher by 4.5% than a year earlier and are 11.6% above August’s 5-year average.

By region, 35.2% of the condos rented were from OCR, 34.1% from the RCR, and 30.8% from the CCR.

Some tenants or landlords may have postponed transactions due to superstition, said Luqman Hakim, chief data & analytics officer at 99.co. The month of August is often referred to as “Ghost Month” or “Hunger Ghost Month.”

July was also an exceptionally active month, with condo rental volume reaching a record high, Hakim said.

“For condos, the combination of lower volume and stable overall rents suggests that demand softened without placing broad downward pressure on prices,” Hakim said.

Regional movements show that tenants remained selective, Hakim added.

Prices are likely to remain broadly stable or move modestly in either direction, evidenced by August volumes remaining above both year-ago levels and historical averages, which suggest underlying demand, Hakim said.

data.title: Over half of SMEs use fintech accounts for business needs: Mastercard
data.description:
About 48% with multiple accounts use them to manage cash flow.

More than half, or 55%, of Singapore's small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) use fintech accounts to meet specific business needs, according to Mastercard.

Amongst those using multiple business accounts, 48% said they do so to manage cash flow, whilst 42% use them to separate domestic and international transactions. 

The payments technology firm said another 41% cited faster payments as a reason for maintaining multiple accounts.

The findings come as SMEs across Asia-Pacific (APAC) use an average of five business tools and four payment methods for business expenses.

Mastercard found that 94% of the respondents are interested in adopting at least one additional business tool they do not currently use, whilst 74% said integrated tools are critical to day-to-day decision-making.

Electronic bank transfers are the most commonly used payment method amongst APAC SMEs at 59%, followed by instant payments at 55%, debit cards at 52%, and credit cards at 47%.

Cybersecurity also remains a concern, with seven in 10 considering protection from cyber threats a high priority. However, only 39% currently use cybersecurity tools.

data.title: Singapore, China expand finance taxonomies to cover transition activities
data.description:
Plans include more green panda bonds and technology-backed sustainable finance. 

Singapore and China will broaden their sustainable finance classifications to cover transition activities, not just green projects. 

The move was one of the key initiatives discussed on 17 September, alongside plans to encourage green panda bond issuance and use technology to support sustainable-finance solutions.

The meeting was held in Nanning and led by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and the People’s Bank of China (PBC), with more than 50 regulatory and industry participants from both markets. 

The two sides discussed biodiversity credits, insurance solutions for climate resilience and adaptation, and carbon markets.

They explored the use of insurance solutions in blended-finance structures to mobilise private capital for sustainable financing, and greater cross-border connectivity between carbon markets.

An industry-led Climate Adaptation and Resilience Roundtable held alongside the meeting covered how adaptation and resilience projects could develop viable revenue models and attract commercial financing.

The taskforce currently has three workstreams covering standards, products, and technology.

MAS and PBC lead the standards workstream, whilst China International Capital Corporation and Singapore Exchange lead products. Beijing Green Exchange and MVGX lead the technology workstream.

data.title: Daily Markets Briefing: STI up 0.45%; Top stock is Yangzijiang Shipbuilding
data.description:

data.title: Majority of SG-listed firms flag physical climate risk in annual reports
data.description:
However, only 22% disclosed details, an MSCI report showed.

Nearly all, or 98%, of Singapore-listed companies assessed by MSCI cited physical climate risk in their annual reports, but far fewer detailed its business impact.

The analysis found that out of over 540 companies, only 22% disclosed in detail how it could, or already had, affected their business.

About 26% of constituents fall under the ‘Higher-Exposure, Lower-Preparedness’ (HELP) category. All of them had at least one modelled adaptation with a positive return.

On a global scale, 81% of companies mentioned physical climate risk, but only 27% provided detailed disclosures.

Across 11,868 Asia-Pacific companies assessed between 2023 and 2025, 88% mentioned physical climate risk, but only 33% outlined specific impacts.

MSCI said adaptation measures could offer significant financial benefits for HELP companies.

About 94% of them had at least one modelled adaptation investment with positive savings on investment, with a median benefit-cost ratio of five times in the first year and 37 times over 30 years, it added.

The report estimated that adaptation measures for these higher-risk assets globally would require about $7.15b (US$5.6b) in investment while potentially avoiding $74.3b (US$58.2b) in losses.

$1 = US$0.78
